introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** As an opinion leader, discuss the impact of brain drain in your society and propose some measures you would take to fight this phenomenon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Greeting and statement of the problem (address of an opinion leader).
2. Impact on health, education, the economy and young people.
3. Causes seen from the migrant's point of view.
4. Five measures to fight the problem.
5. Appeal to the audience and closing thanks.

**Model composition (528 words)**

Fellow citizens, distinguished guests and young friends,

I stand before you as a teacher and as a leader of this community to speak about a wound that is slowly weakening our nation: brain drain, the departure of our best-trained men and women to work in other countries. Every year, doctors, engineers, lecturers and technicians leave Cameroon, and every year the gap they leave becomes harder to fill.

The impact of this exodus is felt in every sector. In our hospitals, one doctor may serve thousands of patients, and rural health centres are run by nurses who have no specialist to consult. In our universities, laboratories lack experienced researchers, and students are taught by overworked lecturers who must also supervise hundreds of dissertations. The state spends huge sums to educate these professionals, only to see them enrich the economies of Europe and America, so that we are in effect subsidising the development of richer nations. The country also loses the inventions, businesses and jobs that these talents would have created, and young people are left without role models who prove that success is possible at home. Besides, the departure of one skilled person often takes with it the training of the colleagues who would have learnt from him.

Why do our best minds leave? Let us be honest. Salaries are low and often paid late. Promotion too often depends on connections rather than merit, and corruption discourages honest effort. Research centres lack equipment, and good working conditions are rare. Meanwhile, foreign employers offer high salaries, modern laboratories and the respect that talent deserves. When a nurse can earn in one month abroad what she earns in a year at home, we cannot blame her for choosing to go. Nobody should be condemned for seeking dignity.

As an opinion leader, I propose the following measures. First, the government should pay a decent and regular salary and reward competence through transparent promotion, so that merit, and not tribe or friendship, opens doors. Second, we must invest in laboratories, libraries, hospitals and reliable electricity, so that professionals can practise their skills here. Third, the state should build bridges with the diaspora by inviting Cameroonians abroad to return for short missions, to train local staff and to invest in local enterprises; many are willing if they are welcomed and not suspected. Fourth, civil society and the media should celebrate those who stay and serve, and community leaders such as myself should mobilise local resources to create scholarships and workplaces for graduates. Finally, we should negotiate with wealthy countries so that, when they recruit our health workers, they compensate us by funding training programmes.

Brain drain cannot be ended by speeches or by laws that forbid people to travel. It will end when our country becomes a place where talent is valued, rewarded and trusted. Let each of us, in our homes, schools and offices, begin to build that country today. Let us not wait for others to build it for us, because it is we who will enjoy it. The choice before us is simple: we can continue to export our talent, or we can create reasons for it to stay.

Thank you.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Ignoring the two tasks (discuss the impact AND propose measures) or the role of an opinion leader speaking to an audience.
2. A list of problems with no concrete, realistic measures, and a style that is too informal for a public address.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).
